blocks.text: OPINI - in modern politics, social media has become a battle arena of public opinion. Like the Groom of the Stool in the time of the British Empire, the role of the dodger is now present in the form of a digital crisis team or social media handlers.
They're on duty to clean up the image of politicians or public figures from various scandals and negative issues that are being issued on social media.
Similar to the Groom of the Stool, this team is in charge of ensuring that the public image of a politician remains clean and well-guarded. They:
One. Removing Negative Content: Managing unprofitable information or deleting destructive digital footprint.
2. Create a new narrative: redirect public opinion by creating a more positive narrative.
3. Confronting an attack on social media opinion with a communication strategy designed to quiet the situation.
According to the studies by Vacratsas and Ambler (1999), "The effectiveness of political imagery is often influenced by how messages are communicated, not only by the content of the message itself."

Just like the Groom of the Stool who enjoys a huge influence because of its closeness with the king, social media maintainers also have access to secrets and political internal strategies. They are not only responsible for managing content, but also the gatekeepers of personal information and political strategies, as described by Enli and Thumm (2012): social media provides a room that allows politicians to personalize their communication, but behind the screen, social media teams have great control over the narratives built.

The existence of a dodger shows that in modern politics, the relationship between a ruler (politician) and a social media team is an interdependent relationship. The public needs them to maintain a reputation, while they're using this closeness to build a career in political communication.

As a reflection, the plagiarism of politics is the modern adaptation of the class of the Groom of the Stool, which remains functioning in trust and influence, but this time in a digital arena. It shows that history repeats itself in a new form, according to the needs of the age.
